why: I checked all six expect lines and their proofs. Five are `run` proofs, and each is a local command at the PR head: the printf pipelines into `node bin/csv2json.js`, with or without `--tsv`, each compared to an exact output string; the `node -e` import of `./src/parse.js` with a stated expected string; and grep on test/, `git diff origin/main -- test/csv.test.js` and `npm test` with exit 0. The git diff compares the PR branch against main, so it works before merge. The README line is a `read` proof of README.md in the PR tree. Every line has a single answer that one reader can check: exact strings, exit codes, whether the test is present, and whether README shows the usage line. No line needs a release, deploy, published page or anything that exists only after merge. Publishing a release is listed as a non-goal.
